questions.text: Network Availability (Uptime): Assess network stability: (1) Average uptime % (2G/3G/4G); (2) Frequency of outages; (3) Mean Time to Recover (MTTR); (4) Impact of load shedding (power outages); (5) Redundancy (ring topology vs linear); (6) Disaster recovery capability; (7) SLA adherence for enterprise.
questions.evidence_required: Network Operations Center (NOC) reports, Power backup logs, Outage incident reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Power is the main cause of downtime. Battery backup theft is common. Fiber cuts from road construction frequent.

questions.text: Coverage Quality & Depth: Assess reach: (1) Population coverage %; (2) Geographic coverage %; (3) Indoor coverage quality; (4) Rural vs Urban disparity; (5) 'Not-spot' identification; (6) Signal strength monitoring; (7) Handover success rate (moving between towers).
questions.evidence_required: Coverage maps (RF plans), Drive test reports, Regulator QoS audits
questions.africa_specific_notes: Rural coverage often depends on USF (Universal Service Fund). Indoor coverage poor in dense concrete slums.

questions.text: Data Throughput & Latency: Assess internet speed: (1) Average download/upload speeds; (2) Latency (ping) consistency; (3) Packet loss rates; (4) Jitter (for VoIP); (5) Throttling policies (Fair Usage Policy); (6) Peak hour performance degradation; (7) International gateway capacity.
questions.evidence_required: Speed test data (Ookla/internal), Latency logs, Bandwidth utilization reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Latency high due to distance from content servers (CDNs). 'Unlimited' bundles often heavily throttled.

questions.text: Voice Quality of Service (QoS): Assess call quality: (1) Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR); (2) Call Drop Rate (CDR); (3) MOS (Mean Opinion Score) for voice clarity; (4) Interconnect success (calls to other networks); (5) VoLTE availability; (6) Echo/Noise levels; (7) SMS delivery reliability.
questions.evidence_required: QoS audit reports, Interconnect logs, CDR analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Dropped calls are a major consumer complaint. Regulators often fine for high CDR.

questions.text: Prepaid Billing Accuracy: Ensure correct deductions: (1) Real-time balance updates; (2) Accuracy of bundle deduction; (3) Prevention of 'disappearing airtime'; (4) Notification of usage (50%, 90% alerts); (5) OOB (Out of Bundle) browsing protection; (6) VAS subscription consent (no auto-subscribe); (7) Refund process for billing errors.
questions.evidence_required: Billing system audit, IN (Intelligent Network) logs, Consumer complaint logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: 'Disappearing airtime' is #1 trust killer. OOB browsing eats credit instantly. VAS auto-subscriptions are predatory.

questions.text: Mobile Money Platform Reliability: For Telco-led fintech: (1) Platform uptime (99.99%?); (2) Transaction speed; (3) SMS receipt delivery time; (4) USSD session stability; (5) App availability; (6) Liquidity management (agent float monitoring); (7) Reconciliation accuracy.
questions.evidence_required: Platform uptime logs, Transaction latency stats, USSD success rates
questions.africa_specific_notes: Mobile Money is life-critical. Downtime stops the economy. USSD timeouts cause double payments/confusion.

questions.text: Power Resilience & Backup: Keeping sites alive: (1) Battery backup autonomy (hours); (2) Generator fuel management (theft prevention); (3) Solar hybrid deployment; (4) Grid availability monitoring; (5) Remote monitoring of power systems; (6) Battery replacement cycle; (7) Resilience to extreme weather.
questions.evidence_required: Power availability logs, Fuel consumption reports, Battery health data
questions.africa_specific_notes: Grid is unreliable. Diesel theft is massive. Solar hybrid is standard for off-grid towers.

questions.text: Physical Security & Vandalism: Protecting assets: (1) Site fencing/security guards; (2) Anti-vandalism sensors; (3) Fiber cut prevention (patrols/marking); (4) Community engagement (to protect sites); (5) Theft recovery rate; (6) Impact of vandalism on uptime; (7) Cyber-physical security.
questions.evidence_required: Security incident logs, Vandalism cost reports, Site access logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Vandalism (batteries, fuel, copper) is a major cost. Fiber cuts by road contractors are frequent.

scoring_notes: Layer 1 (Reliability) for Telecom in SSA: Power is the biggest enemy of uptime. Billing accuracy (airtime) is the biggest enemy of trust. Mobile money reliability is non-negotiable.
